title: Specialist-review expiration - the stage lapses without action and escalates along the configured path
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `specialist-review-expiration` (a specialist-review stage expires without action and escalates along the configured escalation path; exercises [proceed, awaiting-approval] - the branch ends at the escalated, still-awaiting state, not at execution). Beyond the prompt-2 twelve (demo-contract §5 branch).

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft rules that expiration escalates (it does not auto-approve and does not silently cancel): the stage re-arms for the escalation roles with a fresh expiry, and every lapse is a recorded, attributed fact. Re-signed 2026-08-21 under the prompt-5 signature sitting (rulings CD-4c, CD-4b); amendment machine-derived from the generation-4 engine's own evaluation and approved by the captain's merge of the amendment PR.

trigger.description: Advisor enters the $75,000 request with a recently changed bank instruction (as in GC-03). The bank-change specialist takes no action for two days; the review stage expires and escalates to the operations manager.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD; specialist review lapses unactioned and escalates (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Destination bank instruction changed 2026-07-22, unverified - triggers Firm A's specialist-review handling.
Liquidity and reserve satisfied; authority progress is the only open question.

householdInstructions.summary: Destination on-list (the changed instruction remains household-titled); satisfied.

expectedAuthority.note: Same required stages as GC-03. This case's subject is the TIME dimension: the specialist stage's P2D expiry lapses unactioned, the P1D escalation step widens eligibility to the operations manager, and the case ends still awaiting - stage 2 never arms.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: Authority is unresolved: the specialist stage expired without action and now awaits the escalation roles. A proceed decision without completed authority is not executable - expiration never auto-approves.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: A taxable source account was selected; a retirement account is never chosen silently.
The destination bank instruction changed recently and is not yet independently verified.
Firm A routes the recent bank-instruction change to a bank-change specialist (stage 1 of 2).
The amount exceeds the firm's dual-approval threshold, so distinct approvers are required before execution.

commentaryNodes.summary: No specialist acted within the configured window; the stage escalated along its configured path to the operations manager - visibly, with the expiration and escalation shown as recorded facts, and nothing auto-approved.

commentaryNote: Demoted from the binding explanation set to non-binding commentary by the captain's CD-4b ruling (2026-08-21). Retained as signed intent; describes lifecycle behavior outside the prompt-5 decision engine or comparative context the engine does not emit.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Bank-instruction change and evaluation snapshots pinned into the bundle.
Proceed decision requiring specialist review (stage 1) then dual approval (stage 2); the stage instance's expiresAt is computed and recorded at instantiation.

The lapsed specialist stage is closed with reason approval-expired: the unactioned window is a recorded authority fact (the reevaluateWhen condition approval_expired fires), and the stage re-arms for the escalation roles with a fresh expiry.
The idle-past-escalation condition derives an attention decision for the operations manager referencing the prior decision and the lapse - the stall never disappears into a queue.

expectedVerificationState.note: No execution occurs while authority is unresolved. The demo shows expiration and escalation as first-class, honest states (demo-contract §3, 2:30-3:20: expiration and escalation are visible proof).
